patch.value: The duplicate sweep the create protocol mandates refuses to run on this workspace: an all-pairs comparison exceeds its own million-pair bound at 2,467 items and would need 5x10^11 comparisons at the declared million-item target

The project's first Non-Negotiable for creating work is to search existing items and reuse the canonical lineage, and the surface built to answer that question at batch scale does not run here. Measured 2026-08-13 on 2,467 items.

pm duplicates with no filters refuses outright: 'Duplicate sweep exceeded 1000000 candidate pairs; narrow it with statuses or since.' The refusal is correct behaviour against a declared bound and it means the default invocation of the command has no answer on the workspace that the command was built for.

Narrowing shows the shape rather than fixing it. pm duplicates --status closed reports item_count 2,116, candidate_pairs 714,079 and scored_pairs 714,079. That is exactly n(n-1)/2 and scored_pairs equals candidate_pairs, so the sweep is an exhaustive all-pairs comparison with no blocking, no shingling, and no candidate generation of any kind. pm duplicates --status open reports 30,327 pairs for 337 items, the same identity.

Extrapolation against the project's own published scale tiers. At 2,467 items the all-status sweep needs 3,041,811 pairs against a bound of 1,000,000. At 100,000 items it needs 5.0x10^9. At the 1,000,000-item target that pm-o87av6 makes an outcome milestone and pm-9rxu makes an epic, it needs 5.0x10^11 pairs. No constant factor closes that gap; only a sub-quadratic candidate generator does.

Why the closed work does not cover this. pm-2i12ti shipped a batch duplicate-cluster sweep with canonical precomputed similarity signals, and it is not wrong about what it delivered: the per-item signals are precomputed and the scoring is cheap. What was never introduced is a way to avoid scoring most pairs at all. Precomputing the signal reduces the cost of a comparison; it does not reduce the number of comparisons, and the number of comparisons is the term that grows.

The governance consequence is the sharp one. Every agent working here is instructed to check for duplicates before filing, the duplicate-check evidence is recorded in a create-time comment as a matter of convention, and the batch surface that would make that check exhaustive rather than heuristic has been unable to run for as long as the corpus has exceeded 1,415 items. The check that is actually performed is a keyword search, which is a recall-bounded approximation nobody has measured, and pm-p1g43q is the open item that would measure it.

The relationship to the four-command duplicate family matters for sequencing: pm-fmy9ih proposes folding dedupe-audit, dedupe-merge, duplicates and comments-audit into one noun, and consolidating four commands around an algorithm that cannot run at corpus scale would carry the defect into the frozen grammar.

Candidate generation is sub-quadratic: a blocking or locality-sensitive scheme bounds the compared population so the sweep completes at 100k and at 1M items within the published latency tier; The exhaustive path remains available and is declared as such, so a small workspace keeps exact behaviour and a large one keeps a stated recall bound instead of a refusal; The recall of the sub-quadratic scheme is measured against the exhaustive result on a corpus where both can run, and the number is published; pm duplicates with no filters returns an answer on this workspace; The duplicate-check step the create protocol mandates is executable rather than advisory, and the create-time evidence records which mechanism answered
